nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that for every $h > 0$ the function $x \mapsto f(x + h) - f(x)$ is continuous. Then there are functions $g, a : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with $g$ continuous and $a$ additive, that is, $a(x + y) = a(x) + a(y)$ for all real $x$ and $y$, such that $f = g + a$.
nodes.title: De Bruijn's theorem on continuous differences (Erdős Problem 907)

nodes.summary: The statement that every function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $x \mapsto f(x + h) - f(x)$ is continuous for every $h > 0$ can be written as $f = g + a$ with $g : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ continuous and $a : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ additive, that is, $a(x + y) = a(x) + a(y)$ for all real $x$ and $y$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 907
